paras: The lynching of Francis Jordan was the reported killing of a Black woman at Las Vegas, New Mexico Territory, in late 1881, for the alleged murder of a Mrs. Feste. The only known account is a one-sentence item in a Kentucky weekly, which gave no date, no description of who killed her and no circumstances.

According to The South Kentuckian of Hopkinsville, "a negro woman, Francis Jordan, was lynched at Los Vegas, N.M., for the murder of Mrs. Feste." The item did not say when or where in the town the lynching took place, how she was killed, whether she had been arrested, or who took part. Nothing beyond her name was given about Mrs. Feste or the alleged murder.
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage.

The South Kentuckian printed the report on December 6, 1881, as one line in a "General News" column of short national items, between a note that President Arthur had attended a colored Episcopal church on Thanksgiving and a suicide at Fort Omaha. It carried no headline of its own and no comment, and it used the period term "negro woman." No other report of the lynching, from New Mexico or elsewhere, appears in the coverage.
